title: SDK Cookbook: lightweight server & CLI templates with streaming + retry patterns
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create a compact, opinionated cookbook of runnable starter templates and short snippets that demonstrate idiomatic SDK usage for Next.js (TypeScript), FastAPI (Python), Go net/http server, and a cross-language CLI. Focus areas: streaming ergonomics (server and client patterns), robust retry/backoff strategies with idempotency, graceful cancellation and context propagation, token-level cost and telemetry hooks, and small production-ready knobs (timeouts, batching hinting, cache usage). The goal is to provide teams with extremely small, copy-pasteable templates (1-3 files each) that convey best-practices for integrating Redwood Inference SDKs into web frontends, backend servers, and CLIs. Include a short cookbook section with 6 one-off snippets: progressive streaming UI, server-side streaming with background tasks, resumable chunk assembly, exponential backoff examples, retry idempotency token guidance, and a minimal observability hook (emit latency/cost per request to console or metrics). Avoid duplicating existing starter kits; emphasize ergonomics and edge-case handling rather than full boilerplate apps.
acceptance_criteria: Next.js TypeScript example: streaming chat response to client via serverless function + client-side token stream handler; README with 1-line install and usage

FastAPI Python example: async endpoint that proxies streaming tokens from SDK, demonstrates background cache warmup and graceful shutdown; includes example using asyncio.CancelledError for cancellation handling
Go example: single-file net/http server that demonstrates context propagation, request-level timeout, and KV-cache-friendly batched requests to the SDK
CLI example: minimal cross-language pattern (Python and Go) showing progress bar for streaming responses, retry/backoff wrapper, and idempotency token usage
Cookbook snippets: 6 focused recipes with short rationale, code sample, and recommended SDK settings
All examples include comments explaining trade-offs (latency vs batching, cache vs memory), recommended SDK config settings, and link to runtime config options
A single GitHub repo with folder layout and README that reproduces all examples; CI runs linters and a smoke test that validates streaming output for each template
PR reviewed and merged into examples repo, with at least one engineering and one DX reviewer approving
tasks: Draft example flows and file shapes for each template (Next.js api route + client, FastAPI app, Go server, CLI)
Implement streaming helper utilities for TS/JS, Python async iterator wrapper, Go chunk assembler
Write short README and usage snippets for each example with recommended SDK options and environment variables
Add small smoke tests: e.g., run Next dev server, call FastAPI endpoint with sample prompt and assert streaming tokens arrive
Open PR in gitlab/github with CI job that runs smoke tests and linters
Gather feedback from DX and runtime teams, iterate on ergonomics and backoff defaults
